newsitem.title: UK: NWE spot naphtha steady swaps flag gains.
newsitem.headline: NWE spot naphtha steady swaps flag gains.

text.p: NWE naphtha spot prices held steady in quiet trade on Tuesday.
Traders said in the short-term the undertone remained soft with cheaper alternative feedstocks keeping petrochemical buyers relaxed, but forward sentiment indicators, swaps, were slightly firmer.
May swaps firmed $1-$2 a tonne to around $166/$166.50 while June contracts showed similar gains and maintained a $1.50 contango at around $187.50/$188.

Traders said the stronger swaps probably represented perceptions of pick-up in demand from reformers once the U.S. driving season kicks-in and also fresh demand from petrochemical users as the gap to cheaper propane closes.
"Propane is quite a good alternative to naphtha at the moment although the gap is closing," a trader for a major petrochemical company said.
"If you booked the propane around two weeks ago it was worth up to around $16 but that gap is down to below $10 now and looks likely to close further," he added.
One or two late April Russian cargoes were still seen after a 14kt parcel traded into Rotterdam on Monday at a weaker $180 a tonne, around $2 under it's original offer.
